title: Hidden PowerShell opens LSASS with full-access masks and injects a remote thread on scranton
rationale: All describe the same event: PowerShell.exe PID 2976 (pbeesly) on scranton.dmevals.local opened lsass.exe with 0x1F3FFF/0x1FFFFF and a CreateRemoteThread with an UNKNOWN call trace at 2020-05-02T03:05:16Z — LSASS memory access consistent with credential dumping.

title: wsmprovhost.exe on nashua opens LSASS with 0x1F3FFF during pbeesly remote PowerShell session
rationale: Same event on nashua.dmevals.local: wsmprovhost.exe PID 7720 opened lsass.exe with 0x1F3FFF via the PowerShell Management module during pbeesly's Invoke-Command session; LSASS access, though the call trace suggests a PowerShell cmdlet.

title: SAM hive opened with 0xf003f by lsass on scranton
rationale: lsass.exe opened the SAM registry object with 0xf003f during the intrusion window — consistent with local account hash access, though possibly legitimate system activity.

title: Invoke-ScreenCapture loop capturing the desktop every 300s on scranton
rationale: PowerShell script block on scranton defines Invoke-ScreenCapture using Graphics.CopyFromScreen to save full-screen bitmaps every 300 seconds — GUI input capture.

title: Credential-harvesting chain on scranton with pfx export, staging, and PsExec lateral use of pbeesly credentials
rationale: Broader unsecured-credentials activity by pbeesly on scranton (Get-PrivateKeys export, Invoke-Exfil staging, javamtsup.exe service) followed by PsExec to nashua — unsecured credentials.

title: Hardcoded plaintext credentials in attacker PowerShell scripts and staged archive
rationale: Same script blocks on scranton embed plaintext credentials: pfx password 'saribas' and WebDAV account cozy/MyCozyPassw0rd! in Invoke-Exfil (psversion.ps1) — credentials in files.

title: PsExec on scranton launches python.exe on nashua with plaintext pbeesly password
rationale: PsExec64.exe command line on scranton carries cleartext domain credential '-u dmevals\pbeesly -p Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by' to start python.exe on NASHUA — credentials in files/command line.

title: Password-protected archive staged on nashua with hardcoded RAR password
rationale: Rar.exe on nashua run with hardcoded archive password '-hpfGzq5yKw' to create working.zip, then wiped with sdelete64 — credentials in files.

title: Credential-harvesting script on scranton collects password/login-named files into an archive
rationale: PowerShell on scranton enumerated the user profile for *pass*, *login*, *vpn*, *sifr* and similar files and compressed them into Draft.Zip — credentials in files.

title: PowerShell Get-PrivateKeys exports LocalMachine certificates to password-protected .pfx files on scranton
rationale: Same script block (Get-PrivateKeys, readme.ps1, pbeesly, 03:04:56Z) enumerating cert:\LocalMachine and exporting every certificate with its private key via Export-PfxCertificate to Downloads\<random>.pfx — private key theft.

title: accesschk.exe on scranton probes a 'passwordsDB' file in the Sysinternals folder
rationale: accesschk.exe from the attacker-staged SysinternalsSuite created passwordsDB, indicating a password store being touched; no browser credential database access observed.

title: Credential-access intrusion on scranton/nashua without authentication-process modification
No malicious network provider DLL; LSASS memory-write access is the credential-theft signal
Hidden PowerShell compiles .NET payloads with csc.exe from Temp response files on scranton
rationale: csc.exe compiling DLLs from Temp response files under hidden PowerShell is obfuscated/compiled payload execution, not credential access.

title: PsExec-delivered python.exe on nashua beacons to 192.168.0.4:8443 and spawns cmd/powershell
rationale: PyInstaller python.exe on nashua making 348 outbound connections to 192.168.0.4:8443 and spawning cmd/powershell is command-and-control/remote control, not credential access.

title: Screensaver-named loader in C:\ProgramData\victim opens LSA registry key and stages IEX payload on scranton
rationale: explorer.exe launched a .scr loader that opened the LSA registry key, spawned cmd.exe, and wrote monkey.png for the hidden PowerShell stager — user execution of a malicious file, not itself credential access.

title: hostui.exe launched with -verb runas and hostui.lnk placed in StartUp for persistence on scranton
rationale: Elevation via -verb runas and a StartUp-folder shortcut are privilege escalation/persistence, not credential access.

title: sdclt.exe UAC-bypass-style launches from cmd.exe in C:\ProgramData\victim on scranton
rationale: sdclt.exe launched from cmd.exe is a UAC-bypass attempt (bypass user account control), not credential access.
